evidence.claim: Netflix lists categories of personal information it collects about you, beginning with personal details given at registration.
Netflix says it uses personal information to research, analyze and improve its services, including understanding how users interact with the service.
Netflix says it may disclose certain personal information to advertising companies to select ads shown on Netflix, facilitate interaction with ads, and measure and improve their effectiveness.

Netflix says it engages in the sale and sharing of personal information as defined under some US state privacy laws: its use of identifiers for marketing may be considered a 'sale' or 'sharing' under those laws.
A "Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information" link (netflix.com/dnsspi) lets users choose not to have personal information sold or shared.
Netflix may retain personal information as required or permitted by law, including for billing or records purposes; a linked help page covers deletion and retention.

Netflix says its marketing use of identifiers (such as behavioral advertising using cookies and resettable identifiers) may be considered a sale or sharing under some US state privacy laws, and it discloses some information to advertising companies; a Do Not Sell or Share link is provided.

Exodus Privacy static analysis of version 9.84.0 build 3 74548 (report dated Sept. 22, 2026) found code signatures for 1 known tracker SDK(s): Bugsnag (crash reporting). A signature shows the SDK is present, not what data it sends.
